sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – civil law for provincial private and commercial law; common law for federal public, criminal and tax law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU
Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) in force with more than 40 countries

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236–2265; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. For federal corporations only, Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1, but not governing limited partnerships.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport or national identity document for each individual general partner, limited partner and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or licensed lawyer in the partner’s country of residence or origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the country is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the competent Canadian visa office or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of status / certificate of good standing for each corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate registry of the entity’s jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing a Quebec-resident attorney or service agent for service of process and statutory representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in jurisdiction of execution or Canadian notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO structural declaration with ownership chart identifying all natural persons controlling directly or indirectly 25% or more of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal counsel or notary preparing the pre-incorporation file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized; apostille or consular legalization only when the document is relied upon outside Canada or Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution holding the funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized bank officer’s signature; external legalization normally not required unless demanded by the registry or an AML counterparty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding at least 25%, and ultimate beneficial owners against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions, Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and the Criminal Code terrorist entity list. Politically exposed persons, foreign PEPs and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval under FINTRAC guidance on PEPs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises en ligne / Quebec Enterprise Registrar Online Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec limited partnership name must include the mandatory legal ending 'S.E.C.' or 'société en commandite' and must be in French. Non-French terms are permitted only where required by French grammar, as part of a recognized proper name, trademark, or where accompanied by a French descriptive generic. All characters must be transliterated to the standard Roman character set accepted by the registrar.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission / Board when implying government authority
Gouvernement du Québec / Government of Canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is refused, the applicant or its legal counsel may file a written request for review with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the refusal notice, citing the exact statutory objection and proposing a corrected compliant name. If the registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of Québec (civil division) within the applicable limitation period. An unused reservation may be renewed by filing a new 90-day reservation application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted only as an administrative service address if a physical commercial establishment is maintained in Quebec for records, service of process and revenue purposes. A virtual office alone is not sufficient to establish commercial substance for GST/QST registration, payroll obligations or platform payout contracts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-low: approximately 15% per registration cycle for newly registered enterprises, rising to 25% if the partnership claims an office address used by multiple unrelated entities. ISIC 5820 videogame publishing does not trigger a licensing inspection because no statutory license is required in Quebec.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for online name reservation plus prevailing market professional search fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedule and prevailing notarial tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator / legal translation service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document and per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for electronic enterprise registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for customs-drafted Quebec limited partnership and AML/UBO compliance package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provincial and federal tax registrations (Quebec enterprise number, GST/QST, payroll accounts if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm / Revenu Quebec / Canada Revenue Agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registration fee; professional time at prevailing market billing rates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2186 and 2236–2248 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 2, 17, 18, 25–30; Regulation respecting the fees payable for the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 4)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Montréal, Québec (official corporate registry and online Espace Registraire portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) filed in the Quebec Enterprise Register; online form R-1; effective upon issuance of the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ); filing fee CA$110 (approx. USD 82)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership. Capital contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement; a limited partner must contribute money or property (services are not permitted for a commanditaire under art. 2246 C.c.Q.). No escrow account is required by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the General Partner approves the limited partnership agreement of [PARTNERSHIP NAME] including the capital subscriptions of limited partners as set forth therein; (2) That the registered office of the Partnership is established at [registered office address, Québec] and its principal establishment is so designated; (3) That [MANAGER NAME] is appointed Manager with sole signing authority to execute the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to open Canadian bank accounts; (4) That the Manager shall procure all municipal permits and civil defence clearances necessary for the digital publishing offices; (5) That all such acts and filings are hereby authorized and ratified. Dated this ___ day of ______, 20__.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Optional Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Name Search Service and Name Reservation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the REQ online Quebec Enterprise Register to confirm that the proposed LP name (which must include the words 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.') is distinguished from existing names. If full protection is desired, file a 90-day name reservation application and attach the reservation certificate to the subsequent Declaration of Registration.
required_dossiers: Mandate or power of attorney if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the REQ issues written reasons; resubmit with a revised distinguishable name or file a derogation request under the legal publicity framework before the same registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered legal counsel / Notary of the Chambre des notaires du Québec (notarial form advisable if any immovable is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a written partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) that identifies at least one general partner with unlimited liability and one or more limited partners; records cash or property contributions (services are not permitted for limited partners); sets profit and loss sharing, governance, transfer restrictions, and dissolution events. Execute the agreement before filing the Declaration of Registration.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution schedule and proof of subscribed amounts
Draft business plan for digital game publishing via Steam and console storefronts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contractual terms may be cured by supplementary agreement and a declaration of modification filed with the REQ; ensure all partners execute the amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – 'Espace Registraire' online portal (or paper form R-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Declaration of Registration selecting the legal form 'société en commandite'. Disclose the general partner's name and address, the registered office in Quebec, the principal establishment, business activities (software publishing / digital store operations), and the governing law (Quebec). Attest the accuracy, pay the CA$110 filing fee, and submit online. Upon acceptance, the REQ issues the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and a registration attestation.
required_dossiers: Fully executed partnership agreement (kept at registered office for REQ inspection)
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
Resolution of the general partner authorizing registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of deficiency or query, correct the declaration electronically within the prescribed delay (typically 10 days) or file a written response; unresolved queries can be escalated through the REQ review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Inaugural Governance Resolutions and Registered Office Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner of the Limited Partnership (internal governance; REQ filings as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a meeting of the general partner and adopt the pro-forma first resolution (set forth above) approving the partnership agreement, the registered office address, the appointment of the Manager, banking resolutions, and the filing authorization. Open the partnership minute book and partner register at the registered office in Quebec and record all filings and certificates.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first resolution of the general partner
Registered office lease or occupancy agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any governance defect is cured by a supplemental written resolution unanimous among the general partner; file any required REQ updates within 15 days of the change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Permit and Zoning Verification at the Quebec Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal permits department (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Permis et inspections; or the relevant local municipality office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the office lease is within a zoning classification that permits administrative or digital publishing offices. File for any municipal business permit (permis de commerce / permis d'établissement) required by the applicable municipal by-law. No industrial or manufacturing authorization is required because no hardware manufacturing, warehouse, or physical production facility is operated.
required_dossiers: Municipal permit application form and zoning clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused, request written reasons, modify the premises to comply, and re-apply; municipal by-law disputes may be challenged before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety and Occupational Health and Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal fire prevention service (Service de prévention des incendies) and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate for the leased office premises in accordance with the Québec Fire Safety Act and the Québec Building Code (structural and occupancy loads). If employees will be engaged, register the employer with CNESST, adopt a prevention program, and confirm compliance with occupational health and safety requirements before onboarding staff.
required_dossiers: Fire inspection certificate or inspection report
Building lease and occupancy load documents
CNESST employer registration and prevention program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify cited deficiencies promptly and request a re-inspection; CNESST orders may be contested under the Act respecting occupational health and safety within the statutory appeal timeframe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – digital-only publishing of PC and console video games via Steam and PlayStation Store; no industrial plant or manufacturing establishment will be operated in Quebec. The only physical registration is the municipal business permit for the registered office (see Step 5).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industrial operating licence is required. A municipal business establishment permit (permis de commerce) may be required depending on the office location; this is an administrative zoning and occupancy permit, not an industry licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction de l'évaluation environnementale (applicable only were an industrial project contemplated)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Nil – the activity is an office-based digital publishing service with no industrial process, no atmospheric discharge point, no wastewater effluent, and no hazardous waste generation. An EIA is therefore not triggered under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – zero industrial wastewater or VOC emissions. The operation is limited to standard office energy consumption, municipal solid waste collection, and electronics recycling (e-waste) under municipal by-laws; any future hardware warehouse activity would require a new environmental assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the leased office under the Québec Fire Safety Act (CQLR c. S-3.4) and the Québec Building Code (structural and occupancy loads); CNESST occupational health and safety registration and prevention program clearance prior to hiring staff. No civil defense requirements beyond standard fire and workplace safety apply to a digital publishing office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada and, in Quebec, Revenu Québec; combined GST/HST and QST registration is processed through the single-window portal of Revenu Québec for any enterprise with a Quebec establishment, with the federal Business Number (BN) being issued through the CRA Business Registration Online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Form the société en commandite (Limited Partnership) under the Civil Code of Québec and file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) and the partnership's juridical personality. Step 2: Open the partnership's GST/HST (RT) and QST (RQ) accounts with Revenu Québec, which, under the Quebec tax collection agreement, also collects the federal GST on behalf of the CRA; the 9-digit NEQ becomes the single BN-linked identifier used by both tax administrations. Step 3: A non-resident partner without physical presence in Canada may appoint a representative for service and file the non-resident declaration; registration is compulsory once the worldwide taxable-supply threshold of CAD 30,000 is exceeded, but voluntary registration and final-tax returns may be filed immediately to recover input tax credits during the pre-launch build phase of a game studio.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; an LP is fiscally transparent as a matter of statute (Income Tax Act subsection 96(1)). The Quebec LP is simultaneously a separate legal person under the Civil Code of Québec and fiscally transparent at the federal level, producing hybrid-entity characteristics relevant under BEPS Action 2. Available elections affecting tax identity include: (i) Excise Tax Act subsection 177(1) election permitting the partnership to register and account for GST/HST as a distinct person from its members; (ii) Excise Tax Act subsection 273(1) election for a qualifying partner to be the registrant for the partnership's supplies; (iii) Income Tax Act subsection 103(1) election to substantiate a non-pro-rata allocation of partnership income under a reasonable business-purpose basis; and (iv) ETA section 273.1 election for the deemed separate status of the partnership to be disregarded for simplified GST/HST recovery by non-resident partners.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax at 5%) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax at 9.5% imposed on the GST-inclusive sale price), both administered by Revenu Québec for Quebec-establishment businesses and reported on a single return
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in any single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters (the 'small supplier' threshold under ETA section 148 and the parallel QST rule in the Quebec Taxation Act; digital-store sales to Canadian consumers by the LP count toward the threshold, and marketplace facilitation rules deem Valve/PlayStation to collect tax on specified non-resident principal sales, which does not eliminate the LP's own registration duty for direct Canadian revenue)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal or provincial real-time fiscal clearance, SII-style digital stamping, or mandatory B2B API clearance is currently in force for GST/HST/QST in Canada; invoice substantiation follows ETA section 169(4) and QST counterpart provisions requiring supplier name, registration number, and tax amount. Quebec has announced a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing roadmap aligned with the PEPPOL framework for 2027-2030, but it remains proposed rather than enacted; optional PEPPOL and EDI exchange is already accepted as documentary evidence by Revenu Québec.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under ETA Schedule VI, Part V: the supply of intangible personal property (including Steam/PlayStation PC and console game digital licences and publishing rights) to a non-resident recipient is zero-rated where the property is not used in Canada and no service is performed in Canada, and the supply is not made to a Canadian consumer via a Canadian retail presence; corresponding QST zero-rating mirrors the GST rule. For digital-store export sales the LP must establish that the underlying consumer-purchaser is located outside Canada, evidenced by IP/location data on the platform transaction, non-Canadian payment instrument, and contractual licence territory terms.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A export declaration for physical media/collector editions and for controlled digital-asset shipments; no customs declaration applies to pure electronic deliveries via Steam or PlayStation Store)
Bill of Lading (for tangible exports; for digital deliveries the platform licence agreement, digital delivery confirmation, and store settlement reports serve as the transport-substitute document)

Inward Remittance Certificate (Canadian financial institutions do not issue an official IRC; a SWIFT MT103 credit advice or bank account statement showing receipt of USD/CAD payout from Valve or PlayStation Store constitutes the functional equivalent)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess beyond the normal four-year limitation period where a taxpayer has made a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default; denial of zero-rating converts the supply to taxable status and retroactively claws back the GST/QST refund with arrears interest and net-tax deficiency. ETA section 285.1 imposes a minimum penalty of CAD 250 or 25% of the net tax for knowingly making false statements; ETA section 280.1 adds a gross-negligence penalty of 25% of the tax sought; fraudulent refund claims attract criminal liability under ETA section 327.1 and comparable Quebec Taxation Act provisions, with imprisonment on indictment and full return of refunded input tax credits, plus prohibition from continued use of the simplified non-resident GST/HST registration regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority with exclusive authority over monetary policy and currency issuance. Foreign exchange administration is shared with the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act and measures/control instruments applied under the Financial Administration Act. The day-to-day supervision of banking entities is executed by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforces anti-money laundering and terrorist financing obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada maintains no exchange control laws, no quantitative limits on inward or outward remittances, and no prior authorization requirements for foreign direct investment into a Quebec limited partnership. Profit and capital remittances to non-resident partners are freely permitted, subject only to domestic source withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for distributions that are characterized as interest, dividends, rents, royalties, or certain management fees. For partnership allocations, a careful review of the Canadian partnership rules is required because the deemed disposition of a partnership interest or the receipt of a partnership distribution by a non-resident partner may trigger Part XIII withholding unless relief is available under an income tax treaty. In practice, no Bank of Canada approval is needed to convert CAD into USD, EUR, or any other currency for trade or capital purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada does not impose any statutory surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. A Quebec limited partnership engaged in PC and console game publishing via Steam and PlayStation may retain 100% of its export receivables in the original currency of settlement (typically USD or CAD at the storefront payout level). The only operational compliance requirements are: (i) reporting of large international electronic funds transfers (EFT) of CAD $10,000 or more to FINTRAC; (ii) cross-border currency declaration (Form E677 / Canada Border Services Agency) for physical currency or monetary instruments over CAD $10,000; and (iii) standard tax filing of foreign income and deemed taxable Canadian establishments. No deposit of export earnings into a designated government-controlled account is mandatory.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Foreign digital banking platforms and electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury, and Mercury are lawfully accessible to a Canadian limited partnership, but they do not hold a Canadian Schedule I or Schedule II banking license and are not members of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). Their Canadian-facing operations must be registered as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC if they provide transfer services to or from Canada. For a game publisher whose receivables originate from Steam (Valve) and PlayStation Store (Sony), these platforms are useful for low-value, high-frequency pipeline collections, multi-currency virtual accounts, and fast settlement. Legal constraints include: no CDIC deposit insurance above the platform's own banking partner, no formal escrow warehousing capability, no letters of credit or discounting services, and heightened compliance scrutiny if the EMI operates as an unregistered MSB. The cautious blueprint is to maintain a tier-1 Canadian commercial bank account as the primary treasury vault and use a FINTRAC-registered fintech corridor solely as a concentration and conversion gateway for individual storefront payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec limited partnership controlled by non-resident directors or general partners, most Canadian tier-1 banks mandate an in-person identity verification interview for at least one authorized signing officer and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO). Physical presence at a Canadian branch is the default rule; remote opening is permitted only at the discretion of the bank's Global Transaction Banking or Commercial Banking compliance committee and typically requires notarized or apostilled corporate documents, certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and a scheduled video conference with a compliance officer. A Canadian-resident general partner, a registered agent, or a Canadian investment manager can sign account opening documentation, but the UBO must still complete the identification process. In practice, a non-resident principal should plan for a single physical visit to Montreal or Toronto, or execute a Private Bank / International Banking remote onboarding route which includes stricter enhanced due diligence and an increased minimum balance threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: The limited partnership structure is viewed as opaque because the general partner and limited partners are separate legal vehicles and no individual is named as the direct signatory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed limited partnership agreement, the certificate of registration from Revenu Quebec, the register of owners and beneficial owners under the Quebec Business Corporations Act equivalent regime, a written breakdown of voting rights and profit-sharing percentages for each limited partner, and a board resolution from the general partner designating the authorized banking representatives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Cross-border sourcing of high-volume digital gaming revenue from Steam and PlayStation creates perceived money laundering risk because individual end-users are not subject to KYC by the publisher.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the official Steamworks Publisher Payout report and the PlayStation Partner Portal sales reconciliation report, the signed publisher agreement with Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment, bank reference letters from the treasury account used to receive store payouts, and a clear narrative of the revenue waterfall showing that only platform settlement proceeds, not third-party aggregated funds, flow into the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-resident ownership combined with a passive-income profile triggers the appearance of a second generation partnership shell used for tax avoidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the profitability forecast, the ESCROW of active business purpose, the commercial substance documents such as office lease in Quebec, employee payroll registers, development and porting service contracts, and the Canadian tax opinion confirming the limited partnership has no passive status issue under the Quebec and federal Income Tax Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Expected high volumes of FX conversion and cross-border wire transfers that exceed the bank's ordinary activity threshold for an untested new client.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a 12-month cash flow projection, a list of counterparty banking details including SWIFT/BIC and IBAN for all known development partners, copies of any distribution agreements and IP licensing agreements, and an executed attestation that all transfers are trade-related and not for the benefit of unnamed third parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: The entity structure permits inbound capital contributions from jurisdictions that the bank classifies as high-risk or monitored by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide source-of-funds statements (bank transfer receipts, notarized donation/gift letters for limited partner capital contributions), personal tax returns or corporate financial statements of the investing limited partner, a legal opinion from counsel in the originating jurisdiction confirming lawful origin of funds, and a sworn UBO declaration in the bank's prescribed form.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant structure: contributions by non-resident limited partners should be sent to the Quebec LP's Canadian operating account via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CUPC - Capital Contribution to a Limited Partnership' or the equivalent bank-specific beneficiary narrative. For CAD settlement, the rail is the Bank of Canada's Lynx RTGS system through the receiving Canadian bank; for USD, the rail is either the U.S. Fedwire via a Canadian bank's correspondent or an internal book transfer if the bank operates a U.S. clearing desk. Verification requirements include: a capital call memorandum signed by the general partner, the partnership agreement provision governing additional contributions, original bank confirmation evidencing the source account in the remitting jurisdiction, and a certificate of non-resident status (Form NR301 or NR302 where applicable). If inflow exceeds CAD $10,000, FINTRAC reporting applies to the Canadian receiving bank. The bank will also require confirmation that the capital is not intended for speculative investments and will be deployed solely for operating expenses, game development, or IP acquisition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 messages for cross-border disbursements to development studios, middleware vendors, porting houses, and infringement settlements. For significant outsourced milestones, a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) with the Canadian bank as issuing bank and the vendor's bank as advising bank is the appropriate rail to secure delivery obligations. For payments to U.S. merchants, the ACH network or Fedwire can be used as an alternative to SWIFT, using the Canadian bank's correspondent account in the United States. For Valve and Sony payouts inbound, the rails are Steam's ACH/wire payout to a U.S. dollar account held by the LP and PlayStation's PayPal/EFT or wire payout engine; these should be preconfigured on the treasury side to hit the tier-1 Canadian account or the FINTRAC-registered fintech concentration account. All outbound transactions over CAD $10,000 must be captured in the bank's FINTRAC EFT reporting and the LP should retain underlying seller invoices and license agreements for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (forwards with a maturity of up to 24 months in USD/CAD and EUR/CAD)
Rolling spot contracts and FX swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR)
Cross-currency swaps for the purpose of converting fixed-rate foreign currency liabilities into CAD
FX options (European style, purchased vanilla options) for the protection of forecast Steam and PlayStation receipts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible but are operationally unavailable for CAD because the currency is fully convertible and has an active onshore deliverable forward market; NDFs would only be considered for highly exotic illiquid currency pairs outside the scope of the core treasury need

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of the partnership’s registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines of CAD $200–$1,000; persistent failure triggers administrative strike-off and cancellation of registration after formal notice from REQ.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after the partnership’s fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD $25 per day (minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500) per partnership; gross-negligence penalties can be imposed for late, missing, or false filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership unless the partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law, the partnership agreement requires an audit, or lenders/creditors mandate audited financial statements through loan covenants. For this Steam publishing LP, no statutory audit would otherwise be triggered.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS if the partnership is a publicly accountable enterprise; otherwise ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is typically selected for a private limited partnership. The LP must use a consistent, recognized framework for financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration requires a confirmation of all persons with significant control (PSCs) as of the declaration date. Any transfers of partnership interests or shareholdings during the preceding fiscal year that create or modify a 25% or greater ownership or control interest must be reported in the declaration. The protocol includes filing the PSC’s full legal name, date of birth, jurisdiction of residence, and ownership details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, contributions, profit-sharing percentages)
Register of Persons with Significant Control (UBO register)
General Partner’s Corporate Records and Minute Book (if the general partner is a corporate entity)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–15,000 per year (for a full statutory audit if required; compilation or review engagements are typically lower)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Not applicable to the LP itself; the Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent. For corporate partners carrying on business in Quebec, the combined federal + Quebec corporate headline rate is 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs): federal small business deduction lowers the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Quebec small business deduction lowers the provincial rate to 5% on the same threshold; combined effective rate on qualified active business income is 14%. Additional incentives include SR&ED investment tax credits and Quebec interactive digital media or video game production tax credits (tax-exempt credits for eligible labour).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return; filed electronically via CRA 'Represent a Client' portal, EFILE, or approved internet file transfer; accompanied by T5013 Summary and t5013 slips per partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the fifth month after the partnership fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due by May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership name, legal trade name, and CRA business number (BN).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LP's BN and denote the jurisdiction of the principal place of business; non-resident partners are identified by country of residence and Canadian non-resident account number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date (can be any day if the LP has not yet established a calendar year; otherwise December 31).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the LP's regular taxation year-end; for a non-resident partner, do not convert to the partner's home country taxation year in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and 6-digit NAICS/ISIC code; for this scope, use NAICS 511210 / ISIC 5820 (game publishing via digital platforms).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the activity as 'publishing and distribution of digital video games through Steam, PlayStation Store, and other online marketplaces'; no specific non-resident instruction beyond accurate classification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner name, tax account number (social insurance number for individuals, BN for corporations), and percentage of income entitlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must provide a Canadian BN or a non-resident account number; if none exists, a TRC from the home jurisdiction must be retained in the partnership's books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's share of partnership gross income, net income, deductions, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate the share of Canadian-source income to each non-resident partner in accordance with the partnership agreement; Part XIII withholding must be computed on the allocated taxable income if legally required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day for each day late, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per partnership; additional penalties under ITA ss. 162(1) and 163(2) for repeated failure; interest accrues on any unpaid balance; directors of a corporate general partner may be assessed for such amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-15 (Société de personnes / Partnership Information Return) and Relevé 15 (RL-15) slips; filed through Revenu Québec's CLIC system or approved electronic filing service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same as federal: no later than the fifth month after the partnership fiscal year-end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec business number (NEQ) and legal identification of the limited partnership (legal form, date of registration).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the LP's NEQ; if the LP is only carrying on business through a permanent establishment in Quebec, indicate 'extraprovincial' status and confirm whether the LP holds a valid registration under the Quebec Business Corporations Act or Partnership Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income of the partnership for the fiscal period from all sources, including net revenue from digital storefront payouts after platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross Quebec-source revenue; non-resident partners' share must be isolated in the subsequent allocation lines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the partnership's taxable income and tax credits among the partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the share of Canadian/Quebec-source income for each non-resident partner; RL-15 slips must be issued to all Quebec resident partners, while non-resident partners receive an equivalent statement for treaty withholding purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 per partnership, plus compounded daily interest; failure to issue RL-15 slips can result in additional penalties of CAD 500 per omitted slip and reduction of allowable expense claims.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on amounts paid or credited to non-resident partners that are distributed from Canadian-source income of the LP. This is the default rate absent a treaty reduction; it is relevant to the LP because a non-resident partner's distributive share is treated as a Canadian-source distribution, not as a dividend from a corporation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident partner must obtain a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction. The LP must retain the TRC and file Form NR301 (Application for Reduction in the Amount of Tax Withheld) with the CRA (and, where applicable, Form NR302 for reduced withholding on partnership income). If the partner is resident in a treaty country, the treaty rate (e.g., 5%, 15%, or 0% under certain conditions for dividends and interest) may be applied at source; otherwise the LP must withhold the statutory 25% and remit it to the Receiver General on the partner's behalf.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate for interest and royalties is 25%. Under Canada's income tax treaties, the rate is generally reduced: interest commonly to 10% (or 15% under some older treaties), royalties to 10% or 15% (or 0% for certain computer software user payments), depending on the specific treaty and whether the recipient is the beneficial owner. The LP must use the Canada Treaty Text and apply the 'beneficial owner' analysis before applying any reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 (Report on Transactions with Non-Arm's Length Non-Residents) must be filed for any taxation year in which the aggregate value of non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1,000,000. Comprehensive contemporaneous documentation supporting arm's length prices (i.e., a Local File and, at the multinational group level, a Master File) is required when the Canadian taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds CAD 50,000,000, or upon request by the CRA under the 'reasonable efforts' standard.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, the CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 of the Income Tax Act) and the substance-over-form doctrine; a limited partnership used to route digital game publishing income without actual employees, offices, decision-making, or commercial risk can be recharacterized upon audit, especially if treaty benefits are claimed. The LP must have genuine business substance in Quebec (e.g., contractual transfer pricing, local operating staff, and active management) to maintain its status as a fiscally transparent partnership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Concealment of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting or underreporting gross receipts from Steam, PlayStation Store, or other digital platforms; fabricating expense invoices; or hiding a partner's allocation in offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of the understatement of tax under ITA ss. 163(2); accrued interest from the due date; criminal prosecution under ITA ss. 239: on summary conviction a fine of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment, imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for the penalties where they directed, consented to, or acquiesced in the evasion; the court may order civil restitution, asset freezes, travel bans (by order seeking a cross-border movement permit), and imprisonment for fraud-related offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Incomplete Partnership Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file T5013 and Quebec CO-15 by the statutory deadline, filing amended returns late after a partner change, or omitting the allocation schedule for non-resident partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: For T5013: CAD 25 per partner per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; for the Quebec CO-15: an equivalent Revenu Québec penalty; interest is compounded daily; if the failure is made knowingly, a further penalty of up to 50% of the tax referred to in the return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are personally liable to the CRA and Revenu Québec for unremitted source deductions and related penalties under the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act; failure to enforce filing compliance can result in director liability assessment and civil collection against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the LP's payments to a foreign affiliate (e.g., excessive distribution fees or IP royalties paid to a parent company without arm's length benchmarking) or failing to file Form T106 and maintaining contemporaneous Master/Local File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust the LP's income to the arm's length amount and impose a 10% penalty on the net transfer pricing adjustment under ITA ss. 247(3); the underlying corporate partners bear the resulting Part I tax deficiency plus interest; in egregious cases a 50% gross negligence penalty may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved non-arm's length pricing are jointly and severally liable for the adjustment penalty; upon failure to pay, civil enforcement includes asset garnishment, director restitution orders, and a travel ban where the director attempts to flee the jurisdiction; corporate criminal liability can arise under ss. 247(7).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec LP as a conduit solely to invoice Steam and PlayStation payouts, while maintaining no employees, no premises in Quebec, no business records, and claiming treaty benefits (e.g., reduced withholding) on behalf of foreign partners with no actual tax substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can invoke GAAR (section 245) to deny the tax benefits and recharacterize the income; a penalty of 50% of the denied tax benefit is imposed; in cross-border situations, CRA may initiate a Mutual Agreement Procedure making the treaty benefit impermissible and voiding the LP's tax treaty claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are exposed to personal liability under the Canada Business Corporations Act for making false representations during audit; civil restoration, prohibition from acting as a director, travel restrictions, and up to 5 years imprisonment for inducing the creation of a sham company have been judicially upheld in egregious cases.
